extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership (Director), Congress, PPAC members, patent stakeholders (individual inventors, companies, patent practitioners), and other policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria used by the Patent Public Advisory Committee (PPAC) to advise the USPTO Director on patent fees, funding, patent quality, and related policy priorities (including fee-specific recommendations). Intended to evaluate fee proposals and recommend actions to improve patent reliability, examination, and fiscal stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPAC statutory responsibilities for finance
rubrics_metrics.description: By statute, the responsibilities of the PPAC on finance include reviewing and advising the Director on the policies, goals, performance, budget, and user fees of the USPTO; holding a public hearing on the USPTO’s patent fee proposals; and submitting a written report setting forth the committee’s comments, advice, and recommendations following the public hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC must convene public meetings, accept written and oral comments (with prior approval for oral presentations), and publish an Annual Report within 60 days after fiscal year-end. At least one voting member must be an independent inventor and at least 25% must represent small entity patent applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for analyzing the fee adjustment proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the aggregate proposed fee increases involves considering the USPTO’s overall needs to fulfill its mission, including the need to maintain a robust operating reserve, IT and infrastructure investments, examiner staffing and pay, and other mission-critical expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider life-cycle costs of getting and maintaining a patent, impact on applicant behavior (especially small inventors), whether USPTO is prioritizing the right expenditures, operational efficiency, and whether the fee changes are likely to raise expected revenue. Take into account statutory constraints (e.g., appropriations) and recent changes reducing fee revenue (e.g., UAIA discounts) and required pay raises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate aggregate vs. individual fee fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fee increases and new fees should be judged based on fairness, effect on applicant behavior, and whether they will in fact raise expected revenue without unduly burdening small inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate fee increases should be evaluated against USPTO priorities (examination quality, reserves, IT). PPAC explicitly opposed a second across-the-board 5% increase because it places an undue burden on individual inventors and small businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for inflationary adjustments when tied to mission needs
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC generally supports inflationary fee adjustments when they are tied to concrete mission needs (e.g., examiner pay, IT improvements) and when funds will be spent to improve reliability and certainty of patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support contingent on transparency that increased fees will fund examination, training, IT/cloud migration, and other reliability-improving investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating reserves and long-term fiscal stability
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO must maintain long-term fiscal stability, including adequate operating reserves, to avoid depleting reserves during appropriations shortfalls and to sustain examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC recommends Congress: promptly enact appropriations to avoid shutdowns; extend or make permanent USPTO fee-setting authority beyond 2026; appropriate or otherwise address approximately $950M in unavailable collected patent fees; and provide the USPTO greater flexibility in fee setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and effective examination as a primary quality metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely and effective examination protects innovators and the public, ensuring that issued patents are reliable, trustworthy, and high-quality foundations for investment and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination quality depends on skilled examiners, adequate time per case, search capabilities, training, and reliable IT infrastructure (e.g., cloud migration). Investments in search, examination capabilities, and training are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and data integrity (assignments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain transparency of ownership (assignment recordation) because assignment data are key to patent data integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC opposes reintroducing assignment recordation fees because such a fee would impede keeping assignment data up to date and harm data integrity, despite the desire to reduce frivolous submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing applications fee fairness and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees on continuing applications are acceptable only if they do not unduly penalize applicants early in prosecution cycles; PPAC supports continuing application fees only with modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, drop the year-three provision and make the fee applicable only for year 7 or after, because three years is often too short (e.g., PCT cases, backlog areas) to evaluate the need for continuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent fee and pendency considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not impose new fees on design patents until pendency issues are addressed; design patent users are already paying expedited fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prioritizing pendency improvements or legislative options (e.g., maintenance fees) rather than imposing additional fees that could burden users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees must fund examination time
rubrics_metrics.description: Support increases in excess-claims fees only if the public receives assurance that increased fees will be spent on examination and/or giving examiners additional time to evaluate such cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee justification should be clear: applicants paying more for larger claim sets should result in direct additional examination resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Time (EOT) for provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Support decreasing EOT fees for provisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lowering these fees reduces barriers for provisional filings and aligns with promoting broad participation and inclusion in innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) fee fairness and inequitable conduct reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Support IDS fee increases only if coupled with reforms to inequitable conduct law; current case law pressures practitioners to disclose every possible reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional IDS fees are charged, direct funds to allow examiners more time to consider the additional references; PPAC suggests legislative reform to reduce over-disclosure pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) fee conditional on USPTO error
rubrics_metrics.description: Support a fee for requesting patent term adjustment only when the applicant is responsible for the adjustment request; if the USPTO made the error, the applicant should not pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee policy should distinguish between applicant-caused corrections and agency-caused corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Extension fee sizing and small entity impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Support in principle fees for patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 156 (e.g., FDA/USDA related), but evaluate fee jumps carefully so initial costs do not unduly burden start-ups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider tiered or scaled fees to avoid penalizing resource-constrained patentees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Continued Examination (RCE) fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Support raising RCE fees and splitting fees for second and subsequent RCEs so applicants requesting multiple RCEs bear more of the cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC supports recovering costs directly from those requesting multiple RCEs rather than subsidizing them with other fees; note the proposal keeps the first RCE below cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of Action tiered fees to incentivize efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Support tiered fees for suspension of action (higher fees for subsequent suspensions) to encourage efficient applicant behavior; fees for suspensions requested at filing (CPA or RCE) should not be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs associated with suspensions should not be subsidized by other fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to terminal disclaimer fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not impose or increase terminal disclaimer fees because such increases place unfair burdens on filers with limited resources and may incentivize suboptimal prosecution behavior (giving up patent term vs. paying).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC does not agree that a fee increase will reduce examination costs or appeals; increased fees could disadvantage smaller filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional delay petition fee tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Support increasing fees for unintentional delay petitions with tiering (higher fees for longer delays) to reflect USPTO processing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tiered fees align with increased agency costs when deciding petitions with longer delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA trial (PTAB) fee increases for cost recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Support increases to AIA trial fees (e.g., IPR) because costs associated with these proceedings have increased (court cases, inflation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee increases should support aggregate cost recovery for USPTO operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-count limits for PTAB filings (opposed to pay-per-word)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not impose pay-per-word increases; set reasonable word limits and allow petitioners to request additional words with appropriate showing of cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay-per-word favors well-resourced petitioners; even if small inventors receive the same word count, preparing longer papers is costly and burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review of PTAB decisions should remain free
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for Director review of PTAB decisions because Director review should be encouraged to ensure consistency of PTAB decisions and charging may adversely affect individual inventors and small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain Director review as accessible; charging could chill important oversight and consistency efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFCP-a 2.0 (After Final Consideration Pilot) fee fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: The AFCP-a 2.0 fee is problematic because it requires paying without a guaranteed interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC suggests either (a) don’t require a fee unless you can guarantee the applicant will get an interview, or (b) don’t require payment until after the applicant gets an interview. If either enacted, PPAC would support the fee increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent-related risk to evaluate
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify patent-related risk into three main types: (1) Intrinsic patent risk (validity, enforceability, scope, design-around risk); (2) Innovation risk (technology, adoption, execution, market, infringement risk); and (3) Environmental patent risk (judicial, legislative, regulatory changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and fee decisions should consider how changes affect these risk categories and stakeholder perceptions of uncertainty in the patent ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and data-driven assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use patent and demographic data to assess participation in the innovation ecosystem and guide efforts to expand and diversify inventor participation; increase stakeholder engagement (requests for comments, public hearings) in fee-setting and rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC highlights importance of sharing PTAB and examination outcome studies publicly to understand differences and inform continuous improvement; recommended collaboration with other agencies (FDA, USDA, Dept. of Commerce, DOD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize investments that increase reliability and predictability of patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders overwhelmingly favor spending to increase reliability and predictability of issued patents; many would accept higher fees if tied to improved reliability of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priorities include improved search, examiner time/training, PTAB-examiner coordination, guidance on subject matter eligibility, IT modernization, and transparency to restore public confidence.
